questions.question: If in a certain code language ‘BHAI’ is written as ‘2819’, then how will ‘CDGH’ be written in that language?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ee18a7e6c9c120a9ee8d4f7b736bb3eb8644f0023025f54b58cf76c364745566.png] 

The pattern followed is,

For BHAI,

The place value of B is 2

The place value of H is 8

The place value of A is 1

The place value of I is 9

So,

BHAI is written as 2819

Similarly,

For CDGH,

The place value of C is 3

The place value of D is 4

The place value of G is 7

The place value of H is 8

CDGH is written as 3478

Hence, “3478” is the correct answer.

questions.question:
Select the option that is related to the third term in the same way as the second term is related to the first term.

147 : 159 ∷ 167 : ?
questions.solution:
The pattern followed here is,

147 + (1 + 4 + 7) = 147 + 12 = 159

Similarly,

167 + (1 + 6 + 7) = 167 + 14 = 181

Hence, 181 is the correct answer.

questions.question:
Read the given statement and conclusions carefully and decide which of the conclusions logically follow(s) from the statement.

**Statement:**

Only white colour vehicles should be allowed in India for promoting peace.

**Conclusions:**

I. Blue colour vehicles promote peace.

II. White colour vehicles promote peace.

options.text: Either conclusion I or conclusion II follows.
Neither conclusion I nor conclusion II follow

questions.solution:
Conclusion 1: This does not follow, because nothing is mentioned about blue vehicles.

Conclusion 2: This follows, because it is mentioned in the statement that white colour vehicles should be used for promoting peace.

Hence, “only conclusion 2” follows.

questions.question: Five friends A, B, C, D and E bought cars which were priced differently. B's car was costlier than C's car but was less costly than E's car. A's car was costlier than D's car but less costly than C's car. Whose car was the 2nd costliest?
questions.solution:
According to the given information,

B's car was costlier than C's car but was less costly than E's car

E > B > C

A's car was costlier than D's car but less costly than C's car

E > B > C > A > D

B’s car is the second costliest.

Hence, “B” is the correct answer.

questions.question: If B = 2 and BUT = 43 then BOSS = ?
questions.solution:
The pattern followed is,

For B = 2,

The place value of B is 2

And,

For BUT = 43

The place value of B is 2

The place value of U is 21

The place value of T is 20

BUT = 2 + 21 + 20 = 43

Similarly,

For BOSS,

The place value of B is 2

The place value of O is 15

The place value of S is 19

The place value of S is 19

BOSS = 2 + 15 + 19 + 19 = 55

Hence, “55” is the correct answer.

questions.question:
Six persons B, C, D, F, G and H are sitting in a row facing the north.

B and C are sitting at the ends.

F is sitting second to the left of C.

D is adjacent to both B and H.

What is the position of G with respect to F?
questions.solution:
Arranging them according to the given information,

B and C are sitting at the ends. F is sitting second to the left of C.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/5b0514605ac78e29d08d6cda7f0127d2ca776eb69653a993918f343693441a54.png] 

D is adjacent to both B and H.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f2cc5e4d6e307f019e9e8c3ee92ecc61a3b078ef2229d5bde6708f091213ddb5.png] 

‘G’ is immediate right of ‘F’.

Hence, “immediate right” is the correct answer.

questions.question:
Two statements are given, followed by two conclusions numbered I and II. Assuming the statements to be true, even if they seem to be at variance with commonly known facts, decide which of the conclusions logically follow(s) from the statements.

**Statement:**

I. All tables are books.

II. All pens are books.

Conclusions:

I. Some tables are pens.

II. Some books are pens.

options.text: Both conclusion I and conclusion II follow
Either conclusion I or conclusion II follows

questions.solution:
Drawing the Venn diagram,

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/86d46827d0383e5e77f3d766d50c4540365fa29fdba41f4d328e6609c2db748f.png] 

Conclusion 1: Some tables are pens → False (This is definitely false)

Conclusion 2: Some books are pens. → True (This is definitely true)

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/22250002a2801e334fed3711f70f77d8ef5772d3ff039714f6ed3b61f466f91a.png] 

Hence, “only conclusion 2” follows.
